mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within three months indicates a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve due to increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to the positive economic news.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a robust supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals disinflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real income increases and the Federal Reserve may consider easing monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods with sustained CPIAUCSL decline over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a robust demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as both consumer and business confidence improve.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS both increase > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when both HOUST and PAYEMS increase by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a tightening labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both supply and demand factors align.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter.
